decisions.reason: Korean has both 마지막으로 and 까지; BASE keeps only “finally,” SOL only “even.”
decisions.replacement: Timing, speed, strength. And finally, even the point of impact.

decisions.reason: SOL replaces 사실 with “detail,” drops 그 완벽한 한 방, and flattens 틀어박혔다 into a generic landing.
SOL omits 순간 and turns 치켜드는 into a completed “raise.”
Panicked repetition of 명치 reads as “my solar plexus” in English; SOL’s “the solar plexus” sounds like a correction.
“Beat to a pulp” is the natural English collocation for 죽사발 내다.
Dropping complementizer “that” makes the quoted teaching more spoken without changing meaning.
Cleaner split of the supermarket vs Sword Saint contrast and a more spoken close for 틀린 말도 아니고.
SOL drops 모든 걸 and turns 마음이 편안해졌다 into a washed-over sensation.
“Legs gave out” is the natural rendering of 힘이 풀린다; moving “against my will” to the fall is cleaner English.
Subjectless inner thought matches the Korean fragment better than BASE’s added “I.”
SOL weakens 우려했던 일 to “that” and collapses 기절해서 쓰러져 있던 into “passed out on the ground.”
Uses binding Gate Guard Pavilion and keeps 의심이 들 정도다 as “enough to make me wonder,” not “almost wondered.”
하늘이 노랗다 is the sky, not “everything.”
제시했습니다 is “presented,” and 승리 is “win,” not SOL’s “proposed” / “Defeat.”
이기겠지 is a confident thought, not “hope that I might.”
그만큼 혹독했다 is correspondingly more brutal; SOL’s “every bit as brutal” flattens that.
“So many” is the natural English for 뭐 이렇게 많아.
SOL drops 무공 and the 만 (“alone”) limit on what he saw.
BASE keeps 익숙해질 법하면 (“might”) and 튀어나왔다 (“come flying out”).
SOL drops 그 외에도, changes 지금의 구파일방 to “into the ranks,” and replaces 스며들어 with “ingrained.”
“Rooted in” / “his teacher” naturalizes 뿌리는 / 가르친 사람은 without losing the thought’s logic.
SOL drops 물었다 and 만, and adds “from my lips.”
“You could at least” captures the reproach in 살살하시든가 better than BASE’s flat “then.”
살았던 적 있으세요 is experiential “have you ever,” not simple past “did you.”
Uses the required ellipsis character for …….
“Heaved a sigh” is the natural English for 한숨을 푹 내쉬다.
미숙했나 봐요 is a past guess; SOL adds present “still.”
Same 지금까지 살면서 meaning in more natural spoken word order.
Korean has both 매일같이 and 밥 먹듯; BASE keeps only the meal simile, SOL only “daily.”
decisions.replacement: Cheongpung had spent his life sparring daily with the Sword Saint, a Supreme Peak master, as casually as if they were sharing meals. Naturally, he would only have learned how to go all out.

decisions.reason: SOL drops 말을 이었다 and turns 슬픈 눈동자로 into a filling-with-sadness action.
Smoother cause clause for 서툴러서 and the required ellipsis character.
Korean is 무림 (Murim), not 강호; “mountain hermit” fits 자연인 better than “backwoodsman.”
English does not need “and said” before the following line of dialogue.
맞아도 싼 is “deserved to get hit,” and 마음에 담아 두지 않을 is “won’t take it to heart,” not “hold it against you.”
점점 is “better and better”; SOL drops the gradual increase.
맑게 웃었다 is a bright smile, and 언제 그랬냐는 듯이 is “as if that never happened,” not “never been sad.”
하나라도 supports SOL’s “so much as,” but 혀 깨물고 죽어 버릴 is still “bite my tongue and die,” not “kill myself.”
decisions.replacement: “Back off right now. If you lay so much as a fingertip on me, I’ll bite my tongue and die.”

decisions.reason: 있는 힘껏 is “with all my strength,” not the vaguer “no matter how hard.”
손맛 is the satisfying feel of hitting him; BASE’s “you feel the best” is ambiguous.
말하는 본새 is specifically how he said it, not a generic “listen to this guy.”
Keeps 샌드백 and 열심히; SOL adds “crap” and drops the sandbag image.
오르더라 is a retrospective realization, so “kept shooting up,” not present “keeps.”
Leads with the late-acquired Toughness clause in more natural English without changing the catch-up claim.
단기 수련 is short-term training, not “intensive.”
벽호공과 상당한 스탯 상승을 얻었고 is gaining the technique and the stats together.
많이 is “a lot”; “a great deal” stiffens Cheongpung’s spoken line.
Need the ellipsis character, but 예 is polite “Yes,” not casual “Sure.”
별다른 악의가 없다 is “no real malice”; SOL’s “not a trace” intensifies, and “restrained myself” is stiffer than Taekyung’s voice.
“Was relieved, too” is cleaner spoken English for 한편으로는 다행.
Present hypothetical “if he were any stronger” matches 놈이라면 / 답도 없지 better than BASE’s past counterfactual.
반드시 넘어야 할 산 needs “absolutely” and the climb-the-mountain image, not abstract “overcome.”
까지 is “even while facing me”; BASE drops that limiter.
“Let me ask you one thing” is the natural English for 하나만 부탁합시다.
그거면 됩니다 is “that’ll suffice,” closer to “all I need” than “all I ask.”
Keeps 말이 끝나기도 전 and 싸늘한 as “cold”; SOL’s “frigid” intensifies and “rose” weakens the 들불 blaze.
어느새 is “already / before I noticed,” not a simple “now.”
정말 is spoken “really,” not literary “truly.”
Uses the required ellipsis character.
이마를 탁 쳤다 is “smacked his forehead”; SOL’s “smacked himself on” is wordier without gain.
말귀가 어두워서 is a habitual trait, which “I can be” captures.
이제라도 알아들으셨으면 됐 trails off on “that’s enough,” which SOL’s “understand now” drops.
쭉 솟구쳤다 is a long surge of Sword Energy, not a stripped “shot from the blade.”
Fronting “Now” matches 이제 and the delayed-readiness joke.
Uses the required ellipsis character.
BASE turns 열심히 into “do my best”; SOL keeps 열심히 and 있는 힘껏 but weakens 반드시 / 어차피.
decisions.replacement: “Benefactor, I’ll really work hard! Even if I fight you with all my strength, you’re bound to get back up anyway!”

decisions.reason: 너울거리는 is undulating, not SOL’s “surging.”
나도 is “me too”; SOL drops it.
Fragment “fast, sharp strike” matches 일격, and 자 is sequential “and,” not BASE’s contrastive “but.”
기합과 함께 창날이 쏟아졌다 is a volley with a shout; SOL’s singular “spearhead rained” is awkward and slightly off.
Keeps 창을 쥔 자 and the two-sentence 사이사이 hide; SOL’s “wielding it” is ambiguous after “martial art.”
“A smile tugged at his lips” is the natural English for 입가에 미소가 맺혔다, and 창날 is singular.
Korean has both 방긋 웃으며 and 바라봤다; SOL collapses the watching.
SOL’s contraction is better English, but 은인이다 is “the Benefactor,” not “a Benefactor.”
decisions.replacement: Jin Taekyung. They hadn’t known each other long, but he was the Benefactor who had helped Cheongpung in many ways.

decisions.reason: “At their first meeting” is a tighter rendering of 초면에.
“Something so precious” is natural English for 이 귀한 걸; BASE’s “this precious” is calqued.
SOL gets 득실거린다 (“crawling”) but weakens 잔인무도한 and 마음씨도 고왔다; BASE has those but not the swarming verb.
decisions.replacement: Grandfather had been wrong. He had said Murim was crawling with frightening people who were vicious and utterly ruthless, but everyone Cheongpung had met was gentle and kind-hearted.

decisions.reason: 밉지 않았다 is “didn’t dislike,” but 자신의 실수로 is “his own mistake,” not merely “accidentally.”
decisions.replacement: He didn’t even dislike the Senior from the Zhongnan Sect whom he’d injured through his own mistake not long ago.

decisions.reason: Naturalizes the 선배/후배 bond without losing 피보다 진한 / 끈끈한 인연.
그리고 is “and,” not SOL’s “also,” which falsely links this to the previous point.
SOL adds unsupported “deeply” and turns 그런 선배를 into “someone so weak.”
Uses the required ellipsis character.
마음 아플 일이 없어서 is “no reason to feel bad,” with “and” for the paired brothers.
Keeps Cheongpung as the subject of 즐겁기 그지없었다 rather than abstracting the exchange.
웃음을 터트렸다 is “burst out laughing”; SOL is only a synonym swap.
Spoken 좋아서요 is “because I’m happy,” distinct from the earlier thought 재밌다.
위험한 발언 is specifically a dangerous remark, not just “that’s dangerous.”
이미 그 자리에 없었다 is “no longer where he had been,” which sets up the afterimage; SOL’s “already gone” loses the place.
외쳤다 is a shout with a ghost-seeing face; SOL replaces it with a stare and adds “spear.”
저로 말할 것 같으면 is “as for me,” not SOL’s added “humble man”; 보잘것없는 is “paltry.”
decisions.replacement: “Great Hero Cheongpung, as for me, I’ve been barely scraping by in this harsh world with the paltry Jin Family’s Manoeuvre Technique…”

decisions.reason: 이 새끼가? is incredulous question, not a direct “You little bastard!”
Keeps 되려 (“instead”), 창날 as spearhead, and 내리눌렀다 as pressed, not stamped “the blade.”
카가각 is a metallic scrape/grind, not a crack.
들어 올렸다 is “lifted”; SOL’s “heaved” overstates effort before the later swing.
소용없어요 is “it’s no use,” closer than “that won’t work.”
다음 순간 / 부유감 is “next moment” and a floating sensation, not “instant” / “become weightless.”
Tighter action line for 휘둘러진 창대 and 허공을 밟았다 (“treading empty air”).
SOL drops 순간 and turns 중심을 잃은 into “thrown off balance.”
밀려났다 is shoved, and 청풍이 머물던 허공 should stay “where Cheongpung had been,” not Latinate “occupied.”
One concessive sentence; SOL invents a trailing “but even so…”
Spoken “just” is more natural than “merely” for 단순히 힘뿐만이.
Fragment cadence matches the Korean, and 어마어마한 is “tremendous,” not “monstrous.”
Parallel past perfect (“had grown up”) is cleaner grammar for the same facts.
일초반식 of 펼치는 무공 is a move plus half a form of displayed martial arts; SOL drops 무공 and dashes the term unclearly.
“Sharp enough to cut anyone who touched it” is cleaner English for 손을 대면 베일 것 같은 기세.
정반대 is “exact opposite”; SOL is only a synonym swap.
이걸 is “this,” not “it.”
Keeps 아직 and the 임에도 logic that unremarkable arts still produce tension-giving movement.
Toward the addressee, English naturally says “I’m coming to you” for 내가 간다.
모습에서 is “at the sight of,” and 떠올렸다 is “thought of a word,” not “found.”
기어코 물어뜯으려는 is “hell-bent on biting through”; SOL adds “savage” and changes the bite to “tear out.”
더 거대하게 is “even larger”; SOL drops 더.
